subject: colext,   contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels?

messages.author: 510ab88df6cfabe4
messages.subject: colext,   contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels?
parts:
I am attempting to compare the habitat use and location of a species in a large camera grid across seasons.
 I have reason to believe that the habitat type and space use vary between hot and cool seasons.

#R=100 ( 100 sites)
#J=50 ( 50 observational periods)
#T=2 ( 2 primary samples/ seasons - Hot and Cool)

#Make phony data for observations
Hot<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.5),nrow=100,ncol=50)
Cool<-matrix(rbinom(n=100,size=1,prob=0.25),nrow=100,ncol=50)
y<-cbind(Hot,Cool)

# Generate Yearly-Site Covariates
#Based on the other threads in this forum I have ensured that the factor has 2 levels associated with it both "Hot" and "Cool" ( I know there is a more concise way to write this next step, but I am just ensuring that i haven't accidentally missed something)

h<-(matrix("Hot",100,1))
c<-(matrix("Cool",100,1))
h<-factor(h,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
c<-factor(c,levels=c("Hot","Cool"))
season<-data.frame(h,c)

#Generate the unmarkedMultFrame:
umf2 <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,numPrimary=2,yearlySiteCovs = list(season=season))
summary(umf2)

#run the naive mosel- No problem
fm <- colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf2)

However, when I run a model utilizing yearly-site-level covariates, i.e:
fm.1<-colext(~1, ~1,gammaformula = ~season-1, ~1, umf2)

Error massage
Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) : 
  contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels

Based on this thread and otehrs this is to do with the levels in teh factor not being attributed properly. But, if i check the slot for the season:
> class(umf2@yearlySiteCovs$season)
[1] "factor"
> levels(umf2@yearlySiteCovs$season)
[1] "Cool" "Hot" 

So there are 2 levels. I have compared my data structure to that in the vignette and in numerous online examples and I cannot see any difference in data structure. 

 summary(umf2)
unmarkedFrame Object

100 sites
Maximum number of observations per site: 100 
Mean number of observations per site: 100 
Number of primary survey periods: 2 
Number of secondary survey periods: 50 
Sites with at least one detection: 63 

Tabulation of y observations:
   0    1 <NA> 
6200 3800    0 

Yearly-site-level covariates:
  season   
 Cool:100  
 Hot :100 

I am sure its obvious, but any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance

Chris

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: colext, contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels?
parts: Because there are just 2 seasons and the way you've generated the data, you have all of season 1 hot and all of season 2 cold.  In the default model
colext(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf2)
the parameters to be estimated are psi1, gamma, epsilon, and p (from which one can determine psi2).  In the second model
colext(~1, ~1,gammaformula = ~season-1, ~1, umf2)

season is redundant because psi1 and psi2 are the probabilities for the hot and cold seasons, respectively, and psi1 and psi2 can be estimated without knowing what whether season 1 is hot or cold. With 2 seasons and each season having all sites with the same status, there is only one gamma term that can be estimated:  the transition from a Hot season to a Cold season.  There are no Hot -> Hot, Cold -> Hot, or Cold ->Cold possibilities (given the way the data was generated).

If you take the vignette colext example and reduce the time periods to 2, you'll get the same error message.  If you use 3 seasons you'll see that just year 1 and 2 gamma values can be estimated.but the model runs fine.

Jim Baldwin

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: colext,   contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels?
parts:
People,

I am >98% certain that this has been answered already.

But here we go again: with just two primary occasions, you have one single interval in which to measure colonization and extinction. There is no temporal variation in your response, only spatial variation. Therefore, you cannot use yearly site covariates (which are spatio-temporal), ONLY site covariates (which are purely spatial) to explain that variation. That precludes use of your hot-cold season covariate as explanation.

Best regards  --- Marc
